focus: Paired woody-ID lesson: Cannabaceae/Celtis versus Ulmaceae/Ulmus in Central Texas

Cannabaceae.where_to_look_first: Start at the leaf base and venation: Celtis commonly shows three conspicuous primary veins arising from or very near the base, often with an unequal/asymmetric blade base. Then confirm with a fleshy drupe.
core_characters: Woody local taxa are trees or shrubs with alternate, simple leaves.
Venation commonly strongly 3-nerved from the base in Celtis.
Margins may be entire or toothed; texture may be rough/scabrous from cystoliths.
Flowers are small and inconspicuous; unisexual flowers are common in the family.
Celtis fruit is a thinly fleshy drupe with a hard endocarp/stone.
useful_secondary_cues: Hackberry/sugarberry bark can become corky, warty or ridged, but bark is secondary evidence.
Some Celtis taxa are spiny; Ulmus is unarmed.

Ulmaceae.where_to_look_first: Start at the leaf venation: Ulmus has pinnate venation with many lateral secondary veins; at least some secondaries run directly into the serrations/leaf margin. Then confirm with a dry winged samara.
core_characters: Trees or shrubs with alternate, simple, distichous leaves and stipules.
Margins serrate or biserrate in Ulmus.
Venation pinnate, with numerous lateral veins; at least some terminate at the margin/teeth.
Ulmus fruit is a one-winged samara.
Plants are unarmed and lack latex.
useful_secondary_cues: Elm buds, twig architecture and bark help once leaf/fruit characters are established.
Cedar elm can develop conspicuous corky wings on vigorous twigs.

tie_breaker.fastest_when_fruiting: Celtis = fleshy drupe; Ulmus = dry winged samara.
tie_breaker.fastest_when_vegetative: Celtis = usually 3 strong veins from leaf base; Ulmus = pinnate venation with many straight lateral veins reaching teeth/margin.
tie_breaker.warning: Both may have alternate serrated leaves with asymmetrical bases, so asymmetry alone does not separate them.

cards.look_here_first: Hold one leaf flat and trace the veins from the petiole: look for three strong main veins leaving the base.
confirm: Alternate simple leaf, often somewhat asymmetrical at the base.
Three conspicuous basal primary veins are a strong Celtis cue.
Leaf margin may be entire or toothed depending on leaf/plant.
Fruit is a small fleshy drupe containing a hard stone.
Use bark texture only as a secondary cue.
cards.tie_breaker: Against cedar elm: 3-basal-vein Celtis leaf + fleshy drupe versus pinnately veined elm leaf + winged samara.

cards.look_here_first: Trace the very prominent reticulate venation, especially the strong basal veins, then inspect the small drupe.
confirm: Native from western/central United States into Mexico, including Texas.
Celtis laevigata var. reticulata is a homotypic synonym, not a separate current species.
Use netlike secondary/tertiary venation plus the Celtis basal-vein/drupaceous-fruit pattern.
cards.tie_breaker: The family-level elm tie is still fruit + venation: fleshy drupe and basal three-vein pattern versus samara and pinnate elm venation.
cards.taxonomy_action: Master Plant Pool row for Celtis laevigata var. reticulata should remain as a source-history/synonym row but must point to accepted Celtis reticulata and must not generate a duplicate learner.

cards.look_here_first: Hold the leaf to the light and follow the side veins: many pinnate lateral veins run from the midrib toward the serrated margin instead of three dominant veins starting at the base.
confirm: Alternate simple leaves with a conspicuously oblique/asymmetric base.
Pinnate venation; numerous lateral veins extend toward/into the marginal teeth.
Fruit is a dry winged samara, not a fleshy drupe.
Vigorous twigs commonly develop corky wings.
Cedar elm is unusual among local elms in flowering/fruiting in late summer to fall.
cards.tie_breaker: Against hackberry: many pinnate side veins + dry samara. Against other local elms, add leaf size/texture, seasonal flowering and corky twig wings.

taxonomy_cleanup.action: Retain source provenance but do not count or curate as a separate species; point canonical learner to row 211 Celtis reticulata.
